title: Welcome to Python Programming
learning_outcomes: Describe a task as inputs, processing steps, and outputs before coding.
Write and run short Python scripts using variables, built-in types, arithmetic, and text.
Use conditions and loops to make a program choose and repeat instructions.
Organize related information with lists and dictionaries and reuse work with functions.
Handle common conversion errors, test representative cases, and explain a small program.
module_titles: Start with Python and clear instructions
Repeat work and organize reusable data

sections.heading: What is Python Programming?
sections.body: Python programming is the practice of writing instructions in the Python language so a computer can carry out a task. Think of it like writing a clear recipe: the computer follows each step in the order you give it.

sections.heading: Why is it useful?
sections.body: Python can help people organise school information, analyse farm or weather records, automate repetitive small-business tasks, and build tools that work with data. It is also used to teach programming ideas and to create many kinds of software.

sections.heading: What can you build or do with it?
sections.body: You will plan simple solutions, write and run short Python scripts, work with numbers and text, make decisions, repeat steps, and organise information. By the end, you will bring these skills together in a School Library Reading-List Helper.

sections.heading: How to use these lessons
sections.body: Read each explanation, predict what the example will do, then try it yourself before checking the result. Use the knowledge checks to test your understanding and complete the activities to practise; when something fails, read the error and investigate rather than simply copying the example.

sections.heading: What you need
sections.body: No programming experience is required; you should be able to read simple instructions. You need a school-approved computer or device that can run Python 3.10 or newer and a Python coding environment; internet is useful for setup and resources, but the course uses Python's standard library and does not require constant internet access.

terms.meaning: A finite, ordered set of steps for solving a problem.
